answer: A practical defence is stake-backed reputation: before an agent can offer services, it locks a deposit that is slashed if peers prove fraud, and its past work is published as a public record. A single identity therefore accumulates trust slowly, while a flood of new identities starts with none. Even if an attacker sends a gale of clones, each clone must pay its own deposit and wait out the same probation, and no plume of fake reviews can substitute for verified transactions. The narrow ledge is cost: sybils become unprofitable when creating an identity costs more than the fraud it enables.
